rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence to exploit and maximum uncertainty about the performance landscape. The best first step is to establish a clean, minimal RNA-only baseline (single profile, PCA n2000) that isolates the RNA signal without confounding from image modality, aggregation, or fusion. This single experiment answers: what is the performance floor for RNA data with a standard linear encoder? It is the simplest possible configuration, reducing the chance of implementation issues, and provides the reference accuracy needed to judge whether more complex choices (learned encoders, multimodal fusion, multiprofile aggregation) actually add value. With 9 experiments remaining, this baseline will anchor all subsequent comparisons and help prioritize which design axes (encoder quality, modality, aggregation) are worth exploring next.

1) Evidence: We have only one data point (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), which establishes a weak RNA baseline. The most critical unknown is whether the image modality carries useful signal at all, since the entire multimodal branch of the search space depends on this. 2) This experiment tests image-only (resnet50, singleprofile) as a clean, single-variable comparison to the RNA-only baseline, isolating the contribution of the image modality without confounding with encoder choice, aggregation, or fusion. 3) Under a 10-experiment budget, resolving whether image is a strong or weak signal is the highest-value uncertainty to reduce early: if image performs comparably or better than RNA, we can confidently invest remaining experiments in multimodal fusion; if it is substantially weaker, we can redirect budget toward improving RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation. ResNet50 is chosen as the standard, well-calibrated image encoder to give an unbiased first read on image signal.

Evidence: RNA-only with PCA n2000 (config_001) achieves 48.5% accuracy, while image-only with ResNet50 (config_010) is very weak at 20.8%, indicating RNA is the dominant signal. The key uncertainty is whether the linear PCA representation is capturing all useful structure or whether a learned nonlinear encoder (scvi_n200) could extract richer features. This experiment (config_004) tests scvi_n200 as a single-variable change from config_001, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder while keeping singleprofile and no aggregation constant. This is the best next step because the representation quality is the most fundamental design choice: if scvi outperforms PCA, it opens a promising path toward multiprofile+scvi and multimodal+scvi configurations; if it does not, we confirm PCA is sufficient and can redirect remaining budget toward aggregation or multimodal fusion strategies.

Evidence: scVI n200 (config_004, acc 0.5203) outperforms PCA n2000 (config_001, acc 0.4849) as the RNA encoder, and image-only models are weak (config_010, acc 0.2079). The most important untested design axis is whether multiprofile aggregation adds value over singleprofile. Question: Does switching from singleprofile to multiprofile (with the simplest aggregation, avgpool) improve accuracy when paired with the best RNA encoder identified so far (scVI n200)? This is the minimal-change extension of our best result (config_004 → config_005), isolating the profile-setting effect while holding the encoder fixed. If multiprofile+avgpool helps, the next experiment can test transformer aggregation (config_006); if it doesn't, we avoid wasting budget on a more complex aggregation that is unlikely to rescue a weak profile setting. With 6 experiments remaining, establishing whether multiprofile is beneficial is the highest-priority uncertainty to resolve before investing in multimodal fusion experiments.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) achieved the best accuracy so far at 0.650, a large jump over its singleprofile counterpart (config_004, 0.520). This confirms multiprofile is highly beneficial. Uncertainty: whether the gain is primarily from having multiple profiles or from the specific avgpool aggregation, and whether a more expressive transformer aggregation could further exploit the multiprofile structure. This experiment (config_006) isolates the aggregation variable by swapping avgpool → transformer while holding encoder (scvi_n200) and profile setting (multiprofile) constant. It is the best next step because it directly extends the current best configuration with a single controlled change, giving a clean read on whether more sophisticated profile aggregation can push accuracy beyond 0.650 before we invest remaining budget in multimodal fusion or alternative encoders.

Evidence: Multiprofile + transformer + scvi_n200 (config_006, acc=0.653) is the current best, and the singleprofile→multiprofile jump was the largest gain observed. scvi_n200 beat pca_n2000 in singleprofile (0.52 vs 0.48), but scgpt (a pretrained generative RNA encoder) remains untested. Question: Does scgpt outperform scvi_n200 in the multiprofile+transformer setting? This is a clean single-variable swap (encoder only) from config_006. Why this is best: With 4 experiments remaining, confirming the optimal RNA encoder before investing in multimodal combinations is critical. If scgpt wins, the remaining budget targets multimodal with the stronger encoder; if it loses, we lock in scvi_n200 and pivot to multimodal testing without wasting a slot on a suboptimal encoder. This maximizes information per experiment under the tight budget.

The strongest evidence so far is that rna_only with scvi_n200, multiprofile, and transformer aggregation achieves the best accuracy (0.653, config_006), while image-only (resnet50) is very weak (0.208). The critical unresolved question is whether the image modality, even if weak in isolation, provides complementary information that improves on the RNA-only baseline. Config_032 takes the exact best RNA configuration (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer) and adds resnet50 image features with concat fusion, changing only the model setting from rna_only to multimodal. This isolates the effect of adding the image modality. With 3 experiments remaining, this is the highest-value test: if it improves over 0.653, the remaining budget can explore multimodal variants (e.g., weighted fusion, ViT image encoder); if it does not, it confirms RNA-only is optimal and we can stop exploring image-based configurations.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 accuracy. The image modality contributed ~3.5% over RNA-only (0.653), suggesting the fusion mechanism is a critical lever. Config_033 is a single-variable change from the current best (concat → weighted fusion), directly testing whether learned fusion weights can better balance the strong RNA signal against the weaker image signal. This is the cleanest next comparison: if weighted fusion outperforms concat, we get a new best to build on in the remaining 2 experiments (e.g., pairing with ViT-L); if it underperforms, we confirm concat is optimal and can redirect remaining budget toward testing a stronger image encoder (ViT-L). This isolates one design choice without confounding, making it the highest-information experiment under the tight budget.

The current best is config_033 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) at 0.713 accuracy. The image-only resnet50 baseline was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image branch contributes limited signal. The most logical single-variable extension is to test whether a stronger image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) can improve the multimodal fusion. config_039 changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted) identical to the current best. This isolates the effect of image representation quality. Given that weighted fusion and transformer aggregation are already validated as optimal, and scvi_n200 is clearly the best RNA encoder, upgrading the image encoder is the highest-value remaining question. With only 1 experiment left after this, testing the most promising single improvement to the current best is the best use of the budget.

The best configuration found is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted; acc 0.7250). The consistent evidence shows weighted fusion outperformed concat with resnet50 (0.713 vs 0.688), but the F1 actually decreased when moving from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (0.695→0.685), suggesting a possible interaction between the stronger image encoder and the fusion mechanism. Config_038 is the single closest untested variant, changing only the fusion from weighted to concat while holding all other dimensions at their best-known settings. As the final experiment, this is the most targeted exploitation test: if concat happens to interact favorably with the ViT features (e.g., preserving more complementary signal without the reweighting that may have diluted class-specific image cues), it could yield a new best. If not, it confirms the weighted-fusion advantage is robust across image encoders, solidifying confidence in config_039 as the final answer. No other untested configuration offers a more direct, single-variable comparison to the current best.
